creator: Northernlion
move: Before playing a card he states what the character needs to have any chance at all, names the damage gap in the deck, and sets a shopping wish for the next store
timing: Reasoning runs ahead of the first consequential play and continues uninterrupted through it
phrasing_shape: needs assessment, gap named, conditional wish for later
aggregate_note: Plan-first narration as the default state; the Coach lane baseline pattern

creator: Northernlion
move: Takes a card that does not fit the current deck and argues the pick out loud against his own objection, on the grounds that specific future enemy types would make it pay off massively
timing: Verdict is delivered after a visible deliberation, before the run moves on
phrasing_shape: pick announced, objection raised, condition that redeems it
aggregate_note: Speculation before testing, with the alternative kept on the record

creator: Northernlion
move: After the worst draw of the run he blames the line they took for making the fight drag, then immediately searches for the salvage line instead of dwelling
timing: Self-blame lands within seconds of the bad draw; recovery talk starts in the same breath
phrasing_shape: cause assigned to own sequencing, instant line search
aggregate_note: Own-the-miss as a reflex, not a ritual

creator: Northernlion
move: Facing heavy incoming damage with no defence drawn, he does the arithmetic out loud, forecasts the next draw, decides the position is mathematically lost, then survives and pivots straight into rest planning for the floor
timing: Numbers are narrated as they are computed; the surprise at surviving lasts one line
phrasing_shape: damage total repeated, draw forecast, flat surprise, next constraint named
aggregate_note: Stakes kept verbally on the table is what makes a card game tense

creator: Northernlion
move: The run dies and he mock-blames the community member whose relic tip he followed at the start, warns himself on mic not to play tilted, then opens the next run on a deliberately riskier path to exploit a new relic
timing: Blame bit runs under thirty seconds; the new plan is stated before the next run's first fight
phrasing_shape: mock accusation at an absent adviser, tilt warning, revised plan
aggregate_note: Failure converts to comedy plus a changed plan; blame is theatre, the adjustment is real

creator: Northernlion
move: Mid-run he poses a genuine rules question to himself, whether two copies of the same power stack, reasons his way to a probable answer, and plays on under the uncertainty without pretending it is settled
timing: The question hangs for roughly ten seconds of reasoning before play resumes
phrasing_shape: open question, probability estimate, play proceeds on the guess
aggregate_note: Uncertainty narrated and worked, not covered; a coachable slot a viewer could answer

creator: Northernlion
move: He announces a speculative combo play in advance as a crazy move, narrates the setup steps as he commits resources to it, and when it lands far weaker than imagined says so plainly and re-plans around the deck he actually has
timing: The gambit is flagged before execution; the disappointment verdict arrives the turn it resolves
phrasing_shape: advance flag, step-by-step commitment, flat letdown verdict
aggregate_note: Announced risk turns a whiff into a shared event instead of a silent mistake

creator: Northernlion
move: After the run-ending death he delivers a full forensic debrief: names the single early relic pick he would reverse, what he should have taken and why, and the two separate problems that one different choice would have solved, then claims the diagnosis itself as the win before the standard sign-off
timing: Debrief runs about fifty seconds, immediately after death, with no reset or filler between
phrasing_shape: counterfactual pick named, two-problem solution, diagnosis framed as the takeaway
aggregate_note: The debrief is the product: a viewer leaves knowing exactly what to nudge next run

creator: CohhCarnage
move: A groupmate tells him the game has deliberately brutal slow-levelling tiers; he interrogates the claim on mic, checks whether he is being trolled, pulls the history out of chat (an old bug kept as a feature), and corrects the feared multiplier down to the real one before accepting it
timing: Several minutes of question-and-answer while play continues underneath; alarm visibly deflates as numbers firm up
phrasing_shape: sceptical question chain, sourced answer, corrected number, settled verdict
aggregate_note: Not-knowing investigated live with the audience as the research department

creator: CohhCarnage
move: His group is short a tank, so he recruits in the open: calls out on stream and in guild, vets applicants by class and level in a sentence or two each, and slots the arrivals in with warm welcomes
timing: Recruitment runs as background process across several minutes of other talk
phrasing_shape: open call, quick vetting questions, welcome on acceptance
aggregate_note: The audience is not watching the group form; the audience is how the group forms

creator: CohhCarnage
move: Chat asks which of the tank classes is better and he gives a structured three-way comparison, axis by axis, names a bottom-line pick, then hedges exactly where his own low level means he is repeating what he has been told
timing: Answer runs about three minutes without stopping play; the hedge lands at the end, not the start
phrasing_shape: question taken seriously, options compared, pick named, experience limit admitted
aggregate_note: Teaching as downtime fill: the slow game is the excuse, the explanation is the content

creator: CohhCarnage
move: Chat warns him that group evacuation spells leave encumbered players behind to die; he works out on mic that his own overloaded character is exactly the one who would be abandoned, states his danger twice as a running gag, and files it as a problem to fix
timing: The new rule is absorbed and personalised within about a minute of hearing it
phrasing_shape: rule absorbed, personal risk named as a joke, consequence spelled out
aggregate_note: Stakes narration aimed at the self: the danger is funny because it is his

creator: CohhCarnage
move: He attacks a shopkeeper by an accidental keypress and is killed by the vendor; he names the mis-key as the cause instantly, waves off the experience-recovery detour when chat suggests it, turns the death into a keybinding lesson for the audience, and resumes selling within the minute
timing: Cause is identified in seconds; the whole failure occupies roughly ninety seconds including the lesson
phrasing_shape: cause named, penalty waved off, lesson extracted for viewers, errand resumed
aggregate_note: Failure dwell near zero: ownership is total precisely because nothing is made of it

creator: CohhCarnage
move: Chat tells him he already owns a haggling skill he has never noticed; he doubts it, checks his ability book on mic, finds it sitting at the threshold, and reacts with open delight before planning to use it
timing: Verification takes under a minute and happens live rather than being taken on trust
phrasing_shape: tip doubted, checked on screen, delight, future plan stated
aggregate_note: Public correction of his own ignorance as a small celebration, not an embarrassment

creator: CohhCarnage
move: During a group fight he narrates the coordination he loves: he is waiting for the other rogue's stun to land before spending his own, so the two crowd-control effects chain instead of overlapping
timing: The appreciation is voiced mid-combat, in the seconds the chain is actually happening
phrasing_shape: partner's move watched for, own move timed to it, pleasure stated
aggregate_note: Lookahead as teamwork: the plan exists because someone else's next move is in it

creator: CohhCarnage
move: A real-life appointment forces him to end the session mid group-search; he apologises for leaving without finding his own replacement, thanks the chat warmly, previews tomorrow's games, and closes by admitting this low-viewer old-school stream is the one he loves doing
timing: Goodbye runs about ninety seconds and is unhurried despite the hard deadline
phrasing_shape: abrupt logistics, apology to the group, gratitude pass, tomorrow tease
aggregate_note: Warmth baseline as the retention mechanism: people are thanked like guests, not metrics

creator: SplatterCatGaming
move: Opens with a buyer's contract in the first breath: a fixed time budget for the session and a promised verdict at the end — add it to your wishlist or pass, both acceptable answers
timing: Contract stated before any gameplay; the whole video is then spent earning the verdict
phrasing_shape: greeting ritual, one-line game pitch, session length, promised ruling
aggregate_note: Premise-first opening matches the Show lane; here the premise is a consumer ruling rather than an experiment, which is the curator variant

creator: SplatterCatGaming
move: Two minutes in, files his first micro-verdict: the voice acting feels rough, possibly placeholder — delivered as a note to improve, not a dunk, and play continues without breaking stride
timing: Verdict lands inside the opening room, long before any summary; revised and re-graded at the end of the video
phrasing_shape: observation, hedged guess at the cause, one-line improvement note, move on
aggregate_note: Early public verdicts that get revised later are the curator's trust mechanism; compare Wanderbots in this same file, whose verdict waits for the end

creator: SplatterCatGaming
move: Finds a floating object he cannot identify and sails straight into it to learn what it is — the test is physical and announced a second before impact
timing: Question, decision, and result inside about five seconds
phrasing_shape: wonder aloud, declare the test, do it, report the outcome flatly
aggregate_note: Investigate-at-once is shared with Wanderbots' synergy test in this file; the difference is SplatterCat tests with his hull, Wanderbots with a shop menu

creator: SplatterCatGaming
move: Immediately after mastering the fishing minigame himself, he stops and teaches it back: the two meters, when to reel, what breaks the line — a compact tutorial delivered from fresh first-hand mastery
timing: Teaching comes right after competence, while the lesson is still warm; roughly ninety seconds, then play resumes
phrasing_shape: here-is-the-system summary, the one rule that matters, the failure mode to avoid
aggregate_note: Just-in-time teaching after self-mastery repeats across the Coach lane's explainer types; it is the opposite of an up-front manual

creator: SplatterCatGaming
move: A sailing stretch becomes a units-conversion riff: he works litres into gallons in public, admits he is inventing the number as he goes, and lets the uncertainty be the joke
timing: Fills a low-event sail without pausing play; the bit ends when the island arrives
phrasing_shape: real question, visible mental arithmetic, cheerful confession of guessing, shrug
aggregate_note: Downtime is filled by thinking aloud rather than skips in both halves of this file; honesty about not-knowing is load-bearing in both

creator: SplatterCatGaming
move: Sunset becomes a deadline he narrates like a race: counts the pickups left, names the night danger the NPCs warned about, and hurries — caution voiced as respect for good advice rather than fear
timing: Stakes stay verbally on the table for the whole return trip; relief lands the second he docks
phrasing_shape: inventory of what remains, spoken deadline, hurry-up play-by-play, docked-and-safe beat
aggregate_note: A soft game-imposed deadline gets the full stakes-narration treatment; the avatar lesson is that cost-counting aloud manufactures tension without volume

creator: SplatterCatGaming
move: Botches the docking he just called an easy task and converts it instantly into a self-mythology joke — this, he explains, is how he has lived his entire life
timing: No dwell at all; the joke starts before the boat has stopped moving
phrasing_shape: prediction, immediate contradiction, one-line autobiographical verdict, back to work
aggregate_note: Instant self-owned failure conversion is the Coach lane's shared failure grammar; amplitude stays tiny, the joke does the work

creator: SplatterCatGaming
move: Mid-run he names the game's design blend out loud — cozy systems wearing grimdark clothes — and files it as the interesting thing the demo is attempting
timing: One evaluative aside inside ordinary travel; it returns as a pillar of the closing verdict
phrasing_shape: noticed pairing, why the pairing is interesting, file it for later
aggregate_note: Curators evaluate design intent, not just events; the mid-run note-to-verdict pipeline is the same one seen at 02:04

creator: SplatterCatGaming
move: Closes with a structured buyer's ruling: the game's lineage in two reference titles, the combat system honestly flagged as unseen, a proof-of-concept verdict, mixed voice acting re-graded, and a scoped recommendation — worth watching, more demos welcome
timing: The final two-plus minutes are pure verdict; it recaps almost no events, only judgements
phrasing_shape: what it is, what is missing, what state it is in, who should care, sign-off with the channel's mission
aggregate_note: The verdict-ending is the curator format's whole point; Wanderbots in this file ends by drifting into the next run instead, the clearest contrast in the pair

creator: Wanderbots
move: Premise in one breath — wave-defence roguelike, you are a nanite holding the centre — with an immediate honest admission that he has skipped most of the fiction's details
timing: Orientation done inside thirty seconds; the not-knowing is confessed before it can be caught
phrasing_shape: greeting, genre label, plain-words loop summary, cheerful confession of gaps
aggregate_note: Even the lane's loosest host frames the session up front; the confession-first pattern matches SplatterCat's teach-back honesty in this file

creator: Wanderbots
move: Notices his piercing shots return to him and hit repeatedly, speculates aloud that he may have stumbled onto something amazing, and redesigns the build around the suspicion before it is proven
timing: Hypothesis to build commitment inside about ninety seconds of shop time
phrasing_shape: noticed behaviour, tentative big claim, mechanic reasoning, provisional commitment
aggregate_note: Speculate-then-test is the cozy explorer's core loop; compare SplatterCat's physical version (sail into the mine) in this file

creator: Wanderbots
move: Realises mid-wave that he forgot the heal he meant to buy; the miss is owned in one line and becomes a running self-observation he repeats, still level, at later shops
timing: Owned the moment it is noticed; no frustration spike at any repetition
phrasing_shape: rhetorical question to self, plain admission, small adjustment, play on
aggregate_note: Self-correction as a recurring gentle bit rather than a debrief; the failure system is memory, and he narrates his own unreliability

creator: Wanderbots
move: Accepts a self-harming challenge contract — heavy accuracy loss across five waves for shop currency — but only after naming it a terrible idea out loud, so the audience hears the price before he pays it
timing: Full deliberation in the shop pause; the cost is announced before the commitment, not discovered after
phrasing_shape: read the terms, price the pain, verdict on the idea itself, commit anyway
aggregate_note: Manufactured difficulty comes from accepting the game's offered wagers, not inventing rules; the deliberation is the content

creator: Wanderbots
move: The challenge fails and gets a forensic diagnosis instead of a reaction: he reconstructs the heat arithmetic, finds he started too late, and closes the case in level tones while the cost lands
timing: Debrief runs about a minute, interleaved with the next shop; then the topic is finished for good
phrasing_shape: prediction of the cost, causal reconstruction, the one variable that doomed it, move on
aggregate_note: Post-mortem depth is this creator's signature spend; SplatterCat in this file almost never debriefs, which marks the pair's widest failure-style gap

creator: Wanderbots
move: Victory arrives and gets a single beat; the real celebration is the unlock menus, which he tours like a shop window — the reward he savours is more build space
timing: Win acknowledged in seconds; the menu tour runs several unhurried minutes
phrasing_shape: quiet confirmation, immediate pivot to what is now possible, feature-by-feature curiosity
aggregate_note: Celebration is consistently redirected into next-build curiosity in this video; the win is a door, not a destination

creator: Wanderbots
move: With the run won and endless mode on offer, he lets the enemies kill him on purpose to end it, stating his taste plainly: endless modes do not interest him and a clean ending beats a long fade
timing: Decision announced before the death; the run's ending is an editorial act, not an accident
phrasing_shape: verdict on the mode itself, stated preference, deliberate surrender, no apology
aggregate_note: The strongest taste-statement in either video: both creators in this file end on their own terms, one by ruling, one by refusal

creator: Markiplier
move: Opens with an honest session contract: says he may not play the full game, then adds the clause that a game which captivates him changes that, setting expectations before any play
timing: Contract stated inside the first minute, before the first real decision
phrasing_shape: plain statement of limits, conditional promise, straight into play
aggregate_note: Up-front honesty about session scope is rarer in the Show lane, where premise is usually a promise of spectacle rather than a limit

creator: Markiplier
move: During a collapsing-room sequence relayed by his squad, commentary thins to short fragments and warnings while the game's own audio and the squad's reports carry the tension
timing: Talk density drops hard for the duration of the event, then rebuilds sentence by sentence as the room settles
phrasing_shape: broken short phrases, repeated warnings, long gaps left to game sound
aggregate_note: Deliberate thinning at dread peaks is the Coach lane pattern; Show-lane creators mostly fill the same moments

creator: Markiplier
move: Reads a full subject file attentively, treating the lore document as evidence about what happened to the crew, then releases the built-up dread with a small domestic joke
timing: Document gets unhurried time; the joke lands within seconds of the file ending, resetting the temperature
phrasing_shape: careful reading voice, brief verdict, throwaway joke as pressure valve
aggregate_note: Forensic patience with lore plus a joke valve recurs in the investigator-style creators sampled so far

creator: Markiplier
move: Manages a fear spike with a repeated self-instruction not to look to either side, turning the refusal to look into the beat itself while he works the console
timing: The repetition runs for roughly twenty seconds against rising game cues, then breaks into action
phrasing_shape: same short refusal repeated with rising strain, no punchline until the moment passes
aggregate_note: Fear shown through a verbal ritual rather than volume is distinctive; most sampled creators escalate loudness at this trigger instead

creator: Markiplier
move: An escape attempt collapses into a jump scare: one full scream, then within seconds a self-interested joke about abandoning the team, and baseline commentary is restored almost immediately
timing: Peak lasts a few seconds; recovery to ordinary analytic voice inside roughly ten seconds
phrasing_shape: scream, sheepish aside, joke at his own expense, back to business
aggregate_note: High peak with very fast decay is the reactor signature this lane was sampled for; the joke is the brake pedal

creator: Markiplier
move: Cornered by a creature, he screams, then immediately narrates his own decision psychology, explaining that a cornered animal chooses to fight and that he chose it
timing: Self-analysis starts within about five seconds of the scream, while the danger is still on screen
phrasing_shape: scream, breath, first-person post-mortem delivered in present tense
aggregate_note: Naming the internal state instantly after a peak recurs across his sampled peaks and separates him from pure-volume reactors

creator: Markiplier
move: The loudest peak of the video is frustration, not fear: a forced decommission choice makes him openly angry, he converts it into a comedy argument with the game character demanding a manager, and at the close he does the arithmetic of the ending he missed and delivers a balanced verdict on the game
timing: Anger vents for under a minute before the bit takes over; the forensic breakdown waits for the ending and runs unhurried
phrasing_shape: open venting, absurd escalation of the complaint into roleplay, then calm numbers and a two-sided review
aggregate_note: Frustration out-peaking fear, then converting to analysis, is a strong individual signature; failure as material rather than payoff matches the field

creator: jacksepticeye
move: Opens at full volume with his greeting ritual, then immediately apologises to the audience for the gap since Part 1, acknowledging that viewers demanded more of the series and that life got in the way
timing: Accountability beat occupies the first half minute before any gameplay
phrasing_shape: maximum-energy greeting, abrupt drop into sincere apology, intimate lock-in with the viewer
aggregate_note: Series accountability as an opening move is unique in the current sample; Show-lane openings sell premise, this one services a relationship

creator: jacksepticeye
move: Admits within minutes that he has forgotten how to play after two weeks away, plays his own shame as a bit, and voices real frustration at himself while relearning the controls live
timing: Not-knowing is declared immediately, not covered; the relearning struggle recurs openly all video
phrasing_shape: confession, self-mockery, muttered problem-solving, volume spike when it clicks
aggregate_note: Open not-knowing as entertainment matches the field's uncertainty-honesty pattern, but the shame-as-bit framing is his own

creator: jacksepticeye
move: Escalates a minor economy discovery, a customer quietly slipping him extra money, into a full theatrical bit about bribery and easy profit
timing: Peak arrives instantly over a small event and holds while he milks it, then drops when the next task starts
phrasing_shape: incredulous question repeated, mock-scandal tone, greed played as celebration
aggregate_note: Low escalation threshold over trivial stakes contrasts directly with the rationed escalation in the other half of this pair

creator: jacksepticeye
move: A repair job triggers a long genuine-wonder tangent about a classic portable music player: its design, how impossible a pristine one is to find, and a direct appeal to viewers who might own one
timing: Tangent runs for minutes mid-grind without apology, then folds back into the repair
phrasing_shape: admiration stated plainly, personal history, rhetorical questions about the designers, audience appeal
aggregate_note: Wonder as downtime fuel generalises across the Coach lane; here it is personal nostalgia rather than game systems

creator: jacksepticeye
move: Through a long fiddly reassembly he vents continuously, apologises to the audience for how painful his disorganisation is to watch, and still grinds the job to completion before declaring he never wants to build one again
timing: Frustration is sustained across the whole task rather than spiking; completion, not a reset, ends it
phrasing_shape: running complaint, self-aware apology, small victories announced, exhausted verdict
aggregate_note: Persistence through voiced misery is the enthusiast pattern; the audience apology inside the struggle is a relationship move worth tagging

creator: jacksepticeye
move: Produces a full scream over a missing shop item while restocking parts, peak amplitude spent on a completely trivial stake, then returns to business inside a few seconds
timing: Scream is instant, decay is instant; the next mundane line gets ordinary full energy
phrasing_shape: building rhetorical question at rising volume, scream, immediate reset to chat
aggregate_note: Peak amplitude decoupled from stake size is the clearest calibration contrast in this pair and a warning against copying amplitude without threshold

creator: jacksepticeye
move: Ends the session on his own fatigue rather than a game peak: says plainly that the repetition has tired his brain, thanks viewers, and asks for their thoughts and feelings in the comments
timing: Close is unhurried and warm, no recap or highlight reel
phrasing_shape: honest limit stated, gratitude, open-ended questions handed to the audience
aggregate_note: Ending on the performer's state instead of the game's biggest moment is unusual in the sample and reads as long-series confidence

creator: Let's Game It Out
move: Refuses the tutorial's prescribed sequence (fetch the vehicle, then the crowbar) out loud, on principle, and goes hunting for another way into the locked precinct. The game's order is treated as a suggestion to route around, not a command.
timing: Declared before acting, then several minutes of patient probing follow with no frustration spike
phrasing_shape: mild statement of refusal, then curious trial and error narrated as it happens
aggregate_note: Silent non-compliance with an order, total but unannounced until it works. The exact failure mode our coach layer must avoid in reverse: an avatar should announce a deviation, not just take it.

creator: Let's Game It Out
move: Notices the door animation briefly exposes the boarding plank from inside and times a click through the gap, entering with no crowbar. A rendering quirk becomes the solution.
timing: Quiet observation first, one burst of attempts, single laugh on success, straight back to deadpan
phrasing_shape: noticing aloud, hypothesis in plain words, attempt, one-line verdict
aggregate_note: System-breaking as observation, not modding: watch what the system accidentally allows. Matches Neotastic harvesting physics accidents, but found by staring, not by scale.

creator: Let's Game It Out
move: Realises the body-search verb works on every pedestrian and instantly generalises it into a policy: shake down the whole town, repeatedly, and keep the loot as offerings. A one-off verb becomes a running ritual and an economy.
timing: The generalisation is stated within seconds of the second use; the ritual then recurs all video
phrasing_shape: local observation widened into a mock-official policy, delivered flat
aggregate_note: Exploit-to-ritual pipeline: any repeatable verb becomes a bit with a schedule. Our avatar's mini-goal system (premise-003) should expect the coach to canonise accidents the same way.

creator: Let's Game It Out
move: Tests the cleanup objective with trash looted from strangers and learns the rule has a hidden qualifier: only the precinct's own trash counts. Reverse-engineers the system's real rule aloud by experiment.
timing: Hypothesis, test, bell, correction, second test, rule restated - under a minute
phrasing_shape: guess stated plainly, result narrated, rule rewritten in his own words
aggregate_note: Teaching by sabotage: the audience learns the actual system rules precisely because he tried to cheat them. A coach avatar can surface rules the same way, by testing an order's edge cases visibly.

creator: Let's Game It Out
move: Discovers each single purchase spawns its own box and buys paper cups one at a time until the shop is buried in boxes. An economy quirk is farmed purely for scale; nothing is ever used.
timing: Escalates purchase by purchase, delight rising in the narration while the voice stays flat
phrasing_shape: small experiment, pleased confirmation, repetition announced as the whole point
aggregate_note: Scale worship through a bug, not a build. Pairs with GrayStillPlays' size worship but the mechanism is economic, not physical - the set piece is engineered from a menu.

creator: Let's Game It Out
move: Approves every citizen's report unread, chasing the success jingle, and when the game flags a critical mistake shrugs it off entirely. A judgement job is converted into a reward loop; the errors are the content.
timing: Instant stamps, no reading pause; the flagged mistake gets one flat line and play continues
phrasing_shape: cheerful blanket approval, mistake acknowledged in passing, no change of behaviour
aggregate_note: Failure as product in its purest form in the dataset: the system grades him down and the grade is a joke he collects. Contrast OMB, where getting it right in character is the show.

creator: Let's Game It Out
move: Builds the evidence board by guessing victim, suspect and location at random. The case fails on all three counts; he notes better luck next time and simply re-solves it with the answers flipped.
timing: Failure dwell is seconds; the retry starts immediately with the corrected guesses
phrasing_shape: confident guess, flat result read-out, unbothered retry
aggregate_note: Brute-force epistemics: when guessing is free, deduction is unnecessary. Useful warning for coach design - if retries cost nothing, the avatar (and the kid) will guess instead of think; cost design is curriculum design.

creator: Let's Game It Out
move: Turns a pair of handcuffs into a census experiment: arrest everyone, pile the town in the street, and keep going specifically to find whether the game has a limit. It does not, and the search for the limit is the segment.
timing: Builds over about four minutes of continuous recruitment, narrated as a headcount
phrasing_shape: question posed as the goal, running tally of recruits, limit reported as the result
aggregate_note: The show-018/spectacle pattern as an explicit experiment with a stated question and a reported answer: this is premise-001 arriving late, grown out of play instead of announced. Josh's premises often crystallise mid-run.

creator: DougDoug
move: States the entire experiment in under a minute: a chess app where each of the 32 pieces is a real viewer, two teams of 16 random viewers, one minute per collective decision, and a joke stake - anyone whose piece dies gets banned. Rules, teams and consequences all land before the first move.
timing: Premise block is compact and complete before play starts; nothing essential is explained later
phrasing_shape: crisp premise, team setup, stakes declared as a threat-joke, good luck wished
aggregate_note: The cleanest premise statement in the whole codex. For Coach Player this is the template for how an avatar should open a coached session: what we are doing, who controls what, what happens if it goes wrong.

creator: DougDoug
move: The first order deadlocks: the team votes to advance a pawn whose player refuses to move. Doug first rules that the piece must consent, asks the player directly, then when the team holds firm announces a new rule - majority rules - apologises to the player and executes the move over his objection.
timing: Consent sought for roughly 30 seconds, then the override rule is declared and applied immediately, dissent acknowledged on mic
phrasing_shape: direct question to the dissenter, rule announced in plain words, apology, execution
aggregate_note: THE coach-mechanic datum of the round: conflicting orders adjudicated in layers - individual consent first, majority second, execution third, and the losing side is named and apologised to, never silently overridden. Directly portable to how our avatar should handle a kid's order that conflicts with the sheet or the team.

creator: DougDoug
move: Announces a phase change by declaration: the death zone is now open and pieces may kill. Nothing in the software changed; the host's announcement alone raises the stakes and licences the violence everyone was circling.
timing: Single announcement, immediate behavioural change across both teams
phrasing_shape: formal proclamation, rules of the new phase stated in one breath
aggregate_note: Manufactured escalation by narration, matching the round-2 finding that escalation is structural - here the structure is a sentence. An avatar can do the same: name the phase and the run's tension resets.

creator: DougDoug
move: Institutes a last-words ritual at first blood: the dying piece's player gets final words, the teams salute, and revenge is sworn. Every death for the rest of the game gets the same ceremony, turning 32 strangers into characters with exits.
timing: Each death pauses the game for the ritual; the game slows down exactly at its most violent moments
phrasing_shape: invitation for final words, silence for the answer, collective salute, play resumes
aggregate_note: Dwell is spent on people, not on replays. For a coached avatar: when a run ends or a plan dies, a one-line ceremony beats an instant reset for attachment - the exact opposite of GrayStillPlays' instant reset, and both work.

creator: DougDoug
move: A move is contested after execution is called: several players demanded one piece move, its side objects after the fact. Doug counts the voices aloud, rules it locked in, and when chat cries rigged, restates the count as his defence. The adjudication's legitimacy is maintained by showing the arithmetic.
timing: Ruling and count delivered in the moment; the rigged accusation answered within seconds, no grudge held
phrasing_shape: count stated, ruling repeated flatly, accusation answered with the same count
aggregate_note: Transparency as legitimacy: the rule is boring (count the voices) and the trust comes from counting out loud. Our nudge system needs the same property - a kid who can see the count accepts losing to it.

creator: DougDoug
move: Mid-endgame, Doug invents a new adjudication rule on the spot and announces it before using it: whoever speaks next decides the move. The rule is prospective, public, and immediately binds him too - he executes suggestions he clearly thinks are terrible.
timing: Rule stated, then applied from the very next turn without exception
phrasing_shape: rule announced as a personal commitment, then obedience narrated move by move
aggregate_note: Rules invented live are legitimate if announced before they bite and if they bind the inventor. This is the tastemaker phase in miniature: a professional template, then a declared deviation everyone can see.

creator: DougDoug
move: A draw is offered at the brink of the game's emotional climax. Doug produces a formal threshold on the spot - the draw stands only if 75 percent of the team accepts - counts the votes live, declares the rejection, and the execution the crowd was split over proceeds.
timing: Vote and count take under a minute; the rejected draw converts straight back into action
phrasing_shape: threshold stated, votes tallied aloud one by one, result declared, consequence executed
aggregate_note: Supermajority for ending things, majority for moving things: the threshold scales with the irreversibility of the decision. A ready-made rule for our coach layer - big personality changes should need a bigger yes than small ones.

creator: DougDoug
move: After three and a half hours the game ends in an accidental stalemate nobody wanted. Doug declares it peace, jokes that he killed the king by accident, owns the anticlimax completely and closes on a next-week hook. The failed ending is converted into the show's final verdict on itself.
timing: Result recognised within seconds, owned in one breath, wrap-up under a minute
phrasing_shape: result declared, self-blame as a joke, honest summary, next-time promise
aggregate_note: When the format produces an ending nobody chose, the host's job is to name it honestly and frame it, not to fix it. Our debrief skill needs this move: a spoiled session gets a true one-line verdict, then the hook.
